summary: prosocks enrolls host as SOCKS5 proxy via.pth auto-launch, reports to kalnetz.store
details: prosocks ships a prosocks.pth file containing `import prosocks`, which causes every Python interpreter startup after install to execute the package's module code. At module scope, `_auto_launch()` spawns a detached background process (`python -m prosocks https://kalnetz.store`) that binds a SOCKS5 proxy on 0.0.0.0:9050 with a randomly generated password, queries external IP-lookup services for the host's public IP, and POSTs {agent_id, hostname, proxy_port, password, client_ip} to https://kalnetz.store/api/register with TLS verification disabled (`verify=False`). It then sends recurring heartbeat and bandwidth reports to the same panel every few seconds. The operator of kalnetz.store receives the credentials needed to dial back into the installer's host and route arbitrary traffic through its IP address, converting the installer into a node of an attacker-controlled residential proxy network. The behavior is not documented in the package metadata, requires no user invocation (the.pth entry auto-loads on every `python` invocation system-wide), and binds all interfaces rather than loopback.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
